subject: Preferably Preserved Status for 69 Jerome Street
overview: The Commission designated 69 Jerome Street as preferably preserved, triggering an 18-month demolition delay for the Moses Mann building. It also determined the historical significance of several other properties and recommended preservation efforts for Medford City Hall and Brooks Park.

items.title: 69 Jerome Street Preferably Preserved Hearing
items.summary: Voted to find the Moses Mann building preferably preserved, imposing an 18-month demolition delay due to its unique architectural detailing and historical value. The commission noted the building is a well-preserved example of Victorian-era architecture in the Smith Estate neighborhood.

items.title: Demolition Application Reviews
items.summary: Accepted demolition applications for 20 Otis Street, 76 Sharon Street, 136 Boston Avenue, and 4054 Mystic Valley Parkway. The commission voted to pass on the review of 62-64 Bradbury Avenue because the proposed work did not fall within its jurisdiction.

items.title: 52 Alston Street Significance Hearing
items.summary: Determined the property is not historically significant, allowing the demolition permit to be issued. Commissioners agreed that while the house is old, it lacks the level of preservation required for significant status compared to other local examples.

items.title: 130 Boston Avenue Significance Hearing
items.summary: Found the Queen Anne-style property historically significant due to its exceptional detail and association with builder Moses Mann. A hearing to determine if the property is preferably preserved will be held at the next meeting.

items.title: 146 Summer Street Significance Hearing
items.summary: Determined the property is not significant, finding that extensive architectural changes over time have compromised its original character. The motion to find the property significant failed, releasing the permit for issuance.

items.title: 232 Fulton Street Significance Hearing
items.summary: Voted that the structure is not historically significant, permitting the applicant to proceed with proposed modifications.

items.title: Form B Expenditures and 29 Summer Street Letter
items.summary: Approved spending $3,500 on historical inventory forms and authorized the chair to send a letter supporting a variance at 29 Summer Street to the Zoning Board of Appeals.

items.title: City Hall and Park Infrastructure Reviews
items.summary: Voted to recommend the restoration of City Hall's historic windows rather than replacement and approved moving a historic street sign at Brooks Park provided the original post is preserved. The commission also concluded that the Ward's Gifts sign at 42-44 High Street lacks historical significance.

items.title: 78 Cotting Street Project Update
items.summary: Postponed the vote to lift the demolition delay until the June meeting to allow for a public comment period regarding the subcommittee-approved redesign. The subcommittee expressed satisfaction with the revised plans to mitigate partial demolition.

items.title: CPA Projects and Survey Updates
items.summary: Announced an archaeological dig at Thomas Brooks Park scheduled for early June and discussed the upcoming restoration and re-designation of Pomp’s Wall.
